content.comment_body: Hello everyone, does anyone have a logic to determine RPM and direction of rotation using proximity sensors?
It's difficult to assist without further details. You haven't specified which PLC or controller you are using.
Actually, I'm referring to [product_name] [version_no] for your information.
Hi, I've mentioned which controller I am using.
Hello, there are already topics in this forum regarding RPM measurement with [product_name]. Try using the search feature. Also, video examples can be found on Youtube. Here's a helpful link: [url]
Stating only [product_name] [version_no] is not enough. Please share the full article number and the firmware version.

Is this logic valid for calculating RPM? I3 is the proximity sensor input. The engine shaft has four sensing blocks, so one full rotation produces 4 pulses. Displayed value = (counter value/4) x 60 (the counter is reset each second).
What speed range do you expect? There are different methods to measure speed. For lower speeds, one approach works better; for higher speeds, another is preferable.
The maximum shaft RPM is 1500. I've attached an image. I think this logic is simple and efficient, but if anyone has a better suggestion, please share.
That is the correct approach. For 1500 rpm, that's 25 rotations per second, resulting in 100 pulses per second (with 4 pulses per rotation).
